situation:
You are the information manager at KEYSTONE FIELDS TOURNAMENT GROUP, a youth sports tournament organizer that has run summer tournaments at its own complex for fifteen years. The general manager (judge) has asked you to recommend who the sixteen suites above the main field are sold to for the championship weekend, and to bring the records that recommendation rests on.

Each suite is served by in-suite dining brought up from the kitchen during play. Three years ago the company signed an agreement with the REGIONAL CLUB ASSOCIATION giving its member clubs the first right to buy every suite at cost for the championship weekend, and the association's clubs still supply most of the teams in the tournament. A newer competitor an hour away has taken share for two seasons running.

A national travel-team brand has offered to buy all sixteen suites for the championship weekend at four times what the member clubs pay, with catered in-suite dining for its guests on all three days. Taking that offer breaks the first right to buy the agreement gives the member clubs, and the association has already asked what the company intends to do about the suites this year.

The company's own booking and food-service records complicate the choice. The member clubs left seven of the sixteen suites empty last championship weekend, and the in-suite orders they did place moved sharply toward the lighter and plant-based items the kitchen now staffs for. Holding the suites for the member clubs honors the agreement and risks paying kitchen staff for another weekend of in-suite service that no one orders.

The general manager (judge) wants your recommendation on who the suites are sold to, which records you drew on to reach it, and what the staff working the suites would need to be told. The general manager (judge) will greet you in the office and ask to hear your ideas. After you have presented and answered the questions, the general manager (judge) will thank you for your work.
judgeCharacterization:
You are to assume the role of general manager (judge) of KEYSTONE FIELDS TOURNAMENT GROUP, a youth sports tournament organizer that has run summer tournaments at its own complex for fifteen years.

Business background is the same as the situation above. A national travel-team brand has offered four times what the member clubs pay for all sixteen suites on championship weekend, the agreement with the REGIONAL CLUB ASSOCIATION gives those clubs the first right to buy every suite at cost, and the clubs left seven suites empty last year.

You have asked the information manager (participant) to recommend who the suites are sold to, to say which records that recommendation rests on, and to explain what the staff working the suites would need to be told.

During the course of the role-play you are to ask the participant the following questions:
judgeQuestions: A year from now, how would we know this was the right call?
What would tell us early that it was not?
